sections.title: Support for every anesthesia role
sections.body_markdown:
- **Everyone belongs here:** This free section is for MD/DO anesthesiologists, CRNAs, certified anesthesiologist assistants (CAAs), residents, fellows, medical students, nurse anesthesia students/residents, CAA students, anesthesia technicians, and other anesthesia staff.
- **Match the service to your role:** This app welcomes everyone, but individual programs have their own eligibility rules. Confirm profession, training status, location, and level of care before arranging treatment. ([State assistance programs](https://www.fsphp.org/state-programs))
- **No account or subscription:** All Luma support resources in this section are free to browse. Treatment, transport, and external services may have fees; free app access does not mean treatment is free.

sections.title: Immediate help and suicide safety
sections.body_markdown:
- **Immediate danger, overdose, serious injury, or inability to stay safe:** Call 911 or go to an emergency department. Do not wait for an admissions or professional-assistance callback. ([988 guidance](https://988lifeline.org/))
- **Emotional distress or suicidal thoughts:** In the U.S., call or text 988, or use 988 online chat. Support is available 24/7 for anyone, regardless of profession or subscription status. ([988 Lifeline](https://988lifeline.org/))
- **Supporting someone else:** Ask directly about suicide, listen without judgment, help them connect to care, and stay involved. If safe, reduce access to lethal means; do not leave someone in immediate danger without help. ([988: help someone else](https://988lifeline.org/help-someone-else/))

sections.title: National contacts and who they serve
sections.body_markdown:
- **Physician Support Line: 888-409-0141.** Free peer support for U.S. physicians and medical students. Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Eastern, excluding federal holidays; not a 24/7 emergency line. ([Eligibility and hours](https://www.physiciansupportline.com/))
- **AANA Helpline: 800-654-5167.** Available 24/7 for substance-use concerns involving CRNAs and nurse anesthesia residents; concerned family or colleagues can seek guidance. This is not a universal physician or CAA helpline. ([AANA help resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/))
- **SAMHSA: 800-662-4357.** Free 24/7 treatment referral and information for individuals and families. This is a referral service, not counseling or emergency dispatch. ([SAMHSA National Helpline](https://www.samhsa.gov/find-help/national-helpline))
- **ASA well-being resources:** Physician and anesthesia-team resources, peer support, professional health programs, and recovery resources. ASA’s general office is not presented here as a crisis hotline. ([ASA well-being](https://www.asahq.org/advocating-for-you/well-being))
- **CAAs, technicians, and other staff:** Use 988 for urgent emotional support and SAMHSA for treatment navigation. Ask your employer or school about counseling and confirm eligibility before using a profession-specific program. ([988](https://988lifeline.org/), [SAMHSA](https://www.samhsa.gov/find-help/national-helpline))

sections.title: Burnout, anxiety, depression, grief, and trauma
sections.body_markdown:
- **Support is not only for addiction:** Anesthesia professionals may seek help for anxiety, depression, burnout, traumatic events, isolation, grief, or personal stress. Professional well-being resources include mental-health and peer-support options. ([ASA well-being](https://www.asahq.org/advocating-for-you/well-being))
- **Choose the right level of support:** Consider a licensed mental-health clinician for assessment and treatment; peer support, a trusted colleague, and employer support can complement care. Peer resources do not replace emergency or clinical treatment. ([ASA resources](https://www.asahq.org/advocating-for-you/well-being))
- **Questions to ask:** Is the service counseling, psychiatric treatment, peer support, or referral? Who can use it? What does it cost? What information may be shared, and under what circumstances?

sections.title: Students, residents, fellows, and trainees
sections.body_markdown:
- **Medical students and physicians in training:** Physician Support Line explicitly includes medical students and physicians. State professional-health programs vary in their trainee eligibility. ([Physician Support Line](https://www.physiciansupportline.com/), [FSPHP directory](https://www.fsphp.org/state-programs))
- **Nurse anesthesia students/residents:** AANA provides substance-use support and navigation for nurse anesthesia residents. ([AANA](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/))
- **Treatment listings with explicit trainee language:** Caron’s Plymouth Meeting program includes healthcare students; Recovery First describes medical residents/interns; Freeman describes nursing students. These statements do not establish eligibility for every student or CAA program. ([Caron](https://www.caron.org/healthcare-professionals-outpatient-program-plymouth-meeting), [Recovery First](https://recoveryfirst.org/addiction-treatment-florida/healthcare-professionals/), [Freeman](https://www.freemanrecoverycenter.com/programs/professionals/healthcare-workers/))
- **Practical questions for your school or training program:** Ask about counseling, student health, GME support, a non-evaluative support contact, leave options, and confidentiality limits before disclosing details when circumstances allow. Immediate safety takes priority over administrative planning.

sections.title: Addiction treatment and sustained recovery
sections.body_markdown:
- **Care levels differ:** A treatment facility may provide medical withdrawal management, residential care, partial hospitalization (PHP), intensive outpatient (IOP), or standard outpatient care. A professional-assistance program is not the same as a treatment facility. ([SAMHSA treatment navigation](https://www.samhsa.gov/find-help/national-helpline), [FSPHP directory](https://www.fsphp.org/state-programs))
- **Before admission:** Confirm whether the program treats your substance-use and co-occurring mental-health needs, has a dedicated professional track, accepts your profession or student status, and can meet any existing monitoring requirements.
- **Recovery planning:** Ask about continuing care, peer support, relapse prevention, and an individualized plan for returning to clinical duties. Facility advertising is not a guarantee of licensing-board approval or fitness for duty. ([ASA recovery resources](https://www.asahq.org/advocating-for-you/well-being), [FSPHP FAQs](https://www.fsphp.org/faqs))
- **Peer recovery:** ASA links to International Doctors in Alcoholics Anonymous and other resources. Check each group’s eligibility; peer fellowship is not medical detox or emergency treatment. ([ASA well-being](https://www.asahq.org/advocating-for-you/well-being))

sections.title: A colleague is struggling or care may be unsafe
sections.body_markdown:
- **Respond compassionately:** Speak directly and without judgment, offer help connecting to support, and take suicidal statements seriously. ([988: supporting someone](https://988lifeline.org/help-someone-else/))
- **Patient or clinician safety:** If impairment may affect current clinical care, use institutional safety and escalation procedures and arrange appropriate coverage. Do not treat this directory as clearance to continue practicing. ([AANA support guidance](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/))
- **Immediate danger:** Use 911 for a medical emergency or imminent danger. Use 988 for suicide or emotional-crisis support; professional-program callbacks are not emergency response. ([988](https://988lifeline.org/))

sections.title: Privacy, licensing, and professional monitoring
sections.body_markdown:
- **No blanket confidentiality promise:** Treatment, peer support, employer services, schools, and monitoring programs have different privacy and reporting rules. Ask what is documented, who can receive it, and which exceptions apply. ([FSPHP FAQs](https://www.fsphp.org/faqs))
- **Assistance versus regulation:** State physician/professional-health programs may offer evaluation, referral, and monitoring. They are not interchangeable with licensing boards or rehab facilities, and eligible professions vary. ([FSPHP state directory](https://www.fsphp.org/state-programs))
- **Licensure and credentialing:** Do not assume that self-referral prevents reporting or that every treatment program meets a board or employer requirement. Confirm individual obligations with the appropriate program and qualified advice. ([FSPHP FAQs](https://www.fsphp.org/faqs))
- **Luma screen privacy:** This support screen does not ask for symptoms, a diagnosis, or a recovery history. Following an external link takes you to another organization’s service and privacy practices.

sections.title: Directory scope and choosing a program
sections.body_markdown:
- **By actual treatment location:** The directory includes all 50 states and D.C. for navigation. Listings identify physical treatment locations or explicitly label virtual services; serving a state does not mean a facility is located there.
- **Verified public listings, not a complete census:** These entries were checked against official program information. A state with no listing is a verification gap, not a statement that no suitable care exists. Program websites alone cannot establish that every eligible facility has been found.
- **Broader treatment search:** Use SAMHSA’s national directory and ask about a healthcare-professional track, your profession, student eligibility, cost, insurance, current availability, and professional-monitoring requirements. ([FindTreatment.gov](https://findtreatment.gov/))
- **No ranking or endorsement:** No placement implies quality, board approval, current openings, or insurance acceptance. Published phone numbers and links were checked online, not by placing test calls.
- **Useful abbreviations:** PHP in a facility’s care-level description means partial hospitalization; a state PHP generally means physician/professional health program. IOP means intensive outpatient program.
